name: Wojciech Zaremba
milestone_by_age_26: Co-authored 'Intriguing properties of neural networks' (arXiv Dec 2013, ICLR 2014), a foundational paper on adversarial examples in neural networks with 19,000+ citations, while a PhD student at NYU.
early_history_summary: Won IMO silver medal at 18 representing Poland. Studied math and CS at University of Warsaw and École Polytechnique, earning multiple degrees by 2012. Began PhD at NYU under Yann LeCun and Rob Fergus in 2013, interning at Google Brain and FAIR where he co-authored the seminal adversarial examples paper.
family_context_summary: Born to Irena and Franciszek Zaremba in Kluczbork, Poland; parents supported his early science interests but were not technically oriented.
evidence_summary: Zaremba showed exceptional mathematical ability from a young age in Kluczbork, Poland, winning an IMO silver medal at 18. He studied at the University of Warsaw and École Polytechnique before beginning his PhD at NYU under Yann LeCun and Rob Fergus. During his PhD, he interned at Google Brain and FAIR, co-authoring the seminal 'Intriguing properties of neural networks' paper at age 25. His parents were supportive but not technically oriented; his advantage came from institutional access and self-driven academic excellence.
starting_point: Born to Irena and Franciszek Zaremba in Kluczbork, Poland; parents were not technically oriented but supported his early science interests.
current_position: Co-founder of OpenAI, leading GPT and Codex teams; net worth not publicly disclosed.

Attended Harvard then MIT, dropped out in 2010 to join Stripe as a founding engineer (employee #4-5). Became Stripe's first CTO in 2013.

parent_family_domain_summary: Parents were physicians but not in technology; mother actively sought out extracurricular opportunities like math camps and competitions outside North Dakota.
evidence_summary: Brockman grew up on a hobby farm in rural North Dakota with physician parents who supported his academic pursuits. His mother found math camps and competitions outside the state. His connection to the Collison brothers through MIT and his intense work ethic were key advantages.
starting_point: Born to two physician parents in Thompson, North Dakota; grew up on a hobby farm in a rural setting with limited local tech scene.
current_position: Co-founder and President of OpenAI; net worth estimated in hundreds of millions to billions.

name: Demis Hassabis
milestone_by_age_26: Co-designed and lead-programmed the 1994 game Theme Park at Bullfrog Productions at age 17, which sold several million copies and won a Golden Joystick award.
early_history_summary: Chess prodigy from age 4, reached master standard at 13 with Elo 2300. Bought his first computer (ZX Spectrum 48K) with chess winnings at 8, taught himself programming. Finished A-levels at 16, took a gap year at Bullfrog Productions where he co-designed Theme Park with Peter Molyneux at 17. Then went to Cambridge and earned a double first in computer science.
family_context_summary: Born to a Greek Cypriot father (bohemian, singer-songwriter, sold toys from a van) and Chinese Singaporean mother (retail clerk, part-time cleaner) in North London; parents were non-technical and bohemian.
parent_family_domain_summary: Neither parent was technical; father was an aspiring singer-songwriter, mother worked as a retail clerk and part-time cleaner.

evidence_summary: Hassabis was a chess prodigy who reached master standard at 13 and bought his first computer with chess winnings at age 8, teaching himself programming. His parents were bohemian and non-technical. He finished A-levels at 16 and took a gap year at Bullfrog Productions, where he co-designed and lead-programmed Theme Park at 17, a game that sold millions of copies. His early advantage was primarily his prodigious cognitive ability and intense self-driven specialization in chess, programming, and game AI.
starting_point: Born to a Greek Cypriot father (bohemian singer-songwriter) and Chinese Singaporean mother (retail clerk/cleaner) in North London; working-class, non-technical household.

name: Mustafa Suleyman
milestone_by_age_26: Co-founded DeepMind Technologies in September 2010 at age 26, which was acquired by Google for £400 million in 2014.
early_history_summary: Met Demis Hassabis through his best friend (Hassabis's younger brother) as a teenager in London. Attended Queen Elizabeth's School, Barnet. Co-founded Muslim Youth Helpline at 17. Dropped out of Oxford at 19. Worked as policy officer for London Mayor Ken Livingstone, then co-founded Reos Partners. Co-founded DeepMind in 2010.
family_context_summary: Born to a Syrian taxi driver father and English NHS nurse mother in North London; working-class upbringing in subsidized housing; parents separated when he was 16.
parent_family_domain_summary: Parents were not in technology; father was a taxi driver, mother was an NHS nurse.
evidence_summary: Suleyman grew up in a working-class North London family with a Syrian taxi driver father and English nurse mother. He met Demis Hassabis through his best friend (Hassabis's younger brother) and attended Queen Elizabeth's School, Barnet. He dropped out of Oxford at 19 after co-founding the Muslim Youth Helpline at 17. His key advantage was his early connection to Hassabis and his entrepreneurial and activism experience, which complemented Hassabis's technical expertise when they co-founded DeepMind in 2010.

current_position: CEO of Microsoft AI; previously co-founder of Inflection AI and co-founder of DeepMind.

name: Walter Pitts
milestone_by_age_26: Co-authored 'A Logical Calculus of the Ideas Immanent in Nervous Activity' (1943) with Warren McCulloch, proposing the first mathematical model of a neural network (McCulloch-Pitts neuron).
early_history_summary: Self-taught logician from Detroit who taught himself Greek, Latin, and mathematics. At 12, read Russell's Principia Mathematica and corresponded with Russell. Ran away from home at 15 to study at University of Chicago under Rudolf Carnap. Met McCulloch and co-authored the seminal 1943 paper at 20.
family_context_summary: Born into a rough working-class family in Detroit; father was a boiler-maker who wanted him to drop out and work; ran away from home at 15 and never saw his family again.
parent_family_domain_summary: Father and brothers were rough, uneducated characters who regarded Walter as a freak; no domain advantage from family.
primary_early_advantage_tags: self-taught, Principia-Mathematica, Russell-correspondence, Carnap-mentored, McCulloch-collaborator, ran-away-from-home
evidence_summary: Pitts was a self-taught prodigy from a working-class Detroit family who taught himself Greek, Latin, logic, and mathematics. At 12, he read Russell's Principia Mathematica and identified errors, leading to a correspondence with Russell. He ran away from home at 15 to study at the University of Chicago, where he met Rudolf Carnap and later Warren McCulloch. At 20, he co-authored the seminal McCulloch-Pitts paper proposing the first mathematical model of a neural network. His advantages were entirely self-created through intense autodidactic study, with mentorship from Carnap and McCulloch.
starting_point: Born into a rough working-class family in Detroit; father was a boiler-maker who insisted he drop out of school; ran away from home at 15.
current_position: Died in May 1969 at age 46 in Cambridge, Massachusetts; final role: research associate at MIT.

trajectory.event: Read Russell's Principia Mathematica in a Detroit library over three days and identified errors, leading to a correspondence with Bertrand Russell.

Moved to MIT with McCulloch; became a key figure in the cybernetics movement alongside Wiener and von Neumann.
Died in Cambridge, Massachusetts, from complications related to alcoholism and isolation.
